core_obligations: Construct the map: a tangent vector theta yields a pullback map on differentials to the differentials of the dual numbers, and taking sections produces the kappa(x)-linear map xi_theta on the fibre of Omega_{X/S} at x (proof lines 3024-3033).

Reduce: both sides depend only on the scheme theoretic fibre, and replacing X by the spectrum of its local ring at x changes neither the tangent space nor the stalk of the differentials (proof lines 3034-3044).

Finish in the local case: writing an algebra map to kappa[epsilon] agreeing with the residue map modulo epsilon as c plus D times epsilon, the coefficient D is a k-derivation, and the universal property of the module of differentials gives a bijection between such D and kappa-linear maps xi (proof lines 3046-3055).
proof_roadmap: Write down the map from tangent vectors to dual elements (proof lines 3024-3033).
Reduce to the local ring of the fibre (proof lines 3034-3044).
Apply the universal property in the local case (proof lines 3046-3055).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes f: X to S and a point x, the lemma exhibits a canonical isomorphism between the tangent space T_{X/S,x} and the kappa(x)-dual of the fibre of the relative differentials (statement lines 3013-3021). The forward map is constructed from a tangent vector theta, regarded as a map to the spectrum of the dual numbers over the residue field, by pulling back the differentials and taking the induced kappa(x)-linear map (proof lines 3024-3033). The rest is a chain of reductions: both sides only depend on the scheme theoretic fibre, and the local computation may be performed after replacing X by the spectrum of its local ring at x, which leaves both the tangent space and the fibre of the differentials unchanged (proof lines 3034-3044). The final step is the classical local statement: for a local ring over a field, a kappa-linear map from the module of differentials corresponds to a unique k-algebra map to the dual numbers agreeing with the residue map modulo epsilon, through the universal property of the module of differentials (proof lines 3046-3055). The claim is H2: one explicit construction, two harmless reductions and a standard universal-property argument.
